profile.headline: Software Engineer at Woodward McCoach LLC
profile.summary:
Software engineer who primarily focuses on test automation framework design, development, and deployment. When needed I also do embedded development and support.

I am well versed in different test automation methodologies, frameworks, and libraries to support any number of different telecommunication protocols including LTE, fiber optics, wlan, bluetooth, hspa, gsm, high speed electrical interfaces, etc.

positions.title: Software Engineer - Team Lead
positions.description:
Test Infrastructure Automation - automate embedded software testing using custom designed test benches. Debug and develop fixes for embedded software or feedback issues to stakeholders.
Team Lead - organize project efforts between members
positions.insights: Skills: Test Automation Frameworks · Test Automation Tools · Code Review · Git · Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) · Reliability · Fiber Optics · Metrics Collection · Test Automation · Fiber Optic Networks · Test Planning · Automated Software Testing · Linux · Test Suites

positions.title: Network Software Engineer - Omni-Path Architecture
positions.description: Validation of components in the Intel Omni-Path Architecture.

positions.title: System Verification Engineer
positions.description:
I am a system verification engineer at Intel that works on the verification of modem features.  I specialize in IDC, Thermal Management, Audio, corner case test environments as well as others.

I have been project lead for verification on a number of different features on different product lines.  This task involves driving verification from planning to execution as well as designing and writing the test cases in a number of different programming languages.

In addition to being a verification lead, I have also been a member of multiple different cross functional teams that have members across many different production lines at Intel.  This has allowed me to work with people not only at different geographical locations, but with people that work on very different product lines exposing me to many different approaches to different problems.

positions.title: Research Assistant
positions.description:
The objective of my thesis is to evaluate the legacy products offered by current WiMAX providers and assess improvements that can be made. These include: Re-configurable antennas and adaptive modulation and coding (AMC).

Also included in my thesis is the development of a WiMAX based Physical Layer for the new Software Defined Communication (SDC) testbed being developed in the Drexel Wireless Systems lab.

positions.title: Co-op Engineer for Hardware Production Software Development
positions.description:
As an undergraduate engineering Co-op, I was tasked with characterization of CATV box platform objects as well as building and compilation of HDTV cable box platform objects.

In addition to characterization of HDTV cable box images, I was also to develop and modify test applications and hardware systems.  These developments and modifications were necessary to facilitate testing as well as access certain necessary components not otherwise accessible.

positions.title: Senior Design Project: Software Defined Radio Implementation of WiMAX
positions.description:
We developed a physical layer as well as the MAC layer for a WiMAX based software defined radio using the WARP platform.  We also developed the transmitter and receiver needed for our platform that was run off of the Rice University WARP platform analog cards.  We used MATLAB to develop the physical layer which was used to run WARPLab, which is a non-real time data processing test platform that WARP supports.

Final Deliverables:
-Development of a Software Defined Physical Layer for a WiMAX Based System
-Development of MAC Layer
-Development of Radio Daughtercards for the WARP Platform
-Simulink and Matlab Models for the WiMAX Based System
